data.name: Mrunali
data.gender_notes: Mrunali is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Mruna’, meaning 'pleasant' or 'gentle'. This name is associated with the goddess Durga and is believed to bring happiness and good fortune. The name Mrunali carries the meaning “Gentle and pleasant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mrunali usually hope their child will grow to embody gentle and pleasant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Mrunali belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gentle and pleasant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mrunali total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Mrunali' holds a significant place in Hindu culture, as it is derived from the Sanskrit language, which is considered the root of Hindu philosophies and traditions. The name is also associated with the goddess Durga, one of the principal deities in Hinduism, who symbolizes power, protection, and the Mother Goddess. This name is therefore believed to bring happiness, success, and good fortune to the bearer.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, the name 'Mrunali' is believed to signify purity, gentleness, and kindness. It reminds us of the divine qualities of our Source and inspires us to cultivate these qualities within ourselves, bringing us closer to the divine. The name 'Mrunali' also invokes the blessings of the goddess Durga, who is known to protect her devotees, grant them strength, and guide them towards their highest potential.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mrunali signifies the 'imperishable' or 'unyielding' one, symbolizing the inner strength and resilience of the individual bearing this name. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'mruna' meaning 'unyielding' and 'ali' signifying 'one'. This name is a reminder to hold steadfast in the face of life's challenges, fostering the cultivation of inner strength and endurance.

vedic_reference.note: Mrunali is derived from the Sanskrit words mrūdhāni and lālā which mean 'crown of flowers' and 'garland' respectively.

historical_references.reference:
Mrunali was a legendary queen of the Haihayas, a dynasty that ruled parts of central India around the 12th century CE. She is best known for her deep devotion to Lord Vishnu and her role in the Puranic legend of King Bhoj.
Context: Mythology and Religion

Mrunali was also the name of a renowned Hindu scholar from the 13th century CE who wrote commentaries on various religious texts. She is considered one of the earliest female scholars and authors in Hinduism.
